/.title: The Hackathon Playbook
/.description: Battle-tested hackathon strategy from 36+ wins and $100K+ in prizes, by Bill Zhang. Team formation, ideation, execution, pitching, and submission.

/playbook.title: The 7-Phase Playbook
/playbook.description: A battle-tested 7-phase system for winning hackathons: team formation, ideation, validation, execution, pitching, submission, and post-hackathon strategy.

/playbook/team-formation.title: Team Formation
/playbook/team-formation.description: Pick teammates who cover four roles, and build a steady squad if you want to keep winning.

/playbook/ideation.title: Ideation
/playbook/ideation.description: Combine tools and problems you already know into an idea you can build in time.

/playbook/validation.title: Validation
/playbook/validation.description: Test the riskiest part of your idea early, and prep your stack if you're competing to win.

/playbook/execution.title: Execution
/playbook/execution.description: How to spend your hours so you finish with a working demo.

/playbook/pitching.title: Pitching
/playbook/pitching.description: Build your pitch around the demo, and get ready for judge questions.

/playbook/submission.title: Submission
/playbook/submission.description: What to put in your Devpost, README, and demo video, and when to submit.

/playbook/post-hackathon.title: Post-Hackathon
/playbook/post-hackathon.description: Post your project and follow up with people you met, so it keeps helping you after judging.

/non-coders.title: Hackathons for Non-Coders
/non-coders.description: How non-coders win hackathons with AI tools: the proof it works, the setup, the concepts, and the installable AI skills.

/non-coders/proof.title: The Proof
/non-coders/proof.description: The lawyer who won Anthropic's 500-person hackathon, and three others who build with AI.

/non-coders/setup.title: Getting Started
/non-coders/setup.description: What to set up before your first prompt, and the five-step loop you'll repeat for every feature.

/non-coders/concepts.title: Concepts Explained
/non-coders/concepts.description: GitHub, APIs, deploying, and other jargon explained in plain English.

/non-coders/apis.title: Using APIs
/non-coders/apis.description: How to add a service to your app, with worked examples for ElevenLabs voice and a Supabase database.

/non-coders/system-prompt.title: The System Prompt
/non-coders/system-prompt.description: The CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files that set the rules your AI follows every session. One command sets up both.

/non-coders/skills.title: Skills & Commands
/non-coders/skills.description: Slash commands for each stage of a hackathon build, from planning your app to writing its README.

/non-coders/skills/non-coder-mode.title: Non-Coder Mode
/non-coders/skills/non-coder-mode.description: The AI works in small steps and explains each in plain English. It asks before anything risky, like deleting files, and stays on for the rest of the session.

/non-coders/skills/domain-to-spec.title: Domain to Spec
/non-coders/skills/domain-to-spec.description: Interviews you about your field and your idea, then writes AGENTS.md (rules for the AI) and PRD.md (the plan for your app).

/non-coders/skills/quickstart.title: Quickstart
/non-coders/skills/quickstart.description: Runs /domain-to-spec, /scaffold-frontend, and /scaffold-backend (if needed) in one go, pausing once so you can approve the plan.

/non-coders/skills/scaffold-frontend.title: Scaffold Frontend
/non-coders/skills/scaffold-frontend.description: Turns PRD.md into the first version of your app's frontend in a client/ folder: Next.js pages, navigation, types, and an optional client for your backend.

/non-coders/skills/scaffold-backend.title: Scaffold Backend
/non-coders/skills/scaffold-backend.description: Builds a FastAPI backend in a server/ folder, with sample data for each route PRD.md lists and optional Supabase. Skips itself if PRD.md says no backend.

/non-coders/skills/v0-prompt-crafter.title: v0 Prompt Crafter
/non-coders/skills/v0-prompt-crafter.description: An alternative to /scaffold-frontend. It turns PRD.md or a one-line idea into a paste-ready Vercel v0 prompt, with a visual style researched for your industry.

/non-coders/skills/feature-builder.title: Feature Builder
/non-coders/skills/feature-builder.description: Run it once for each feature. It shows you the plan first: the files and commands it will use, how to test the result, and how to undo it.

/non-coders/skills/bugfix-doctor.title: Bugfix Doctor
/non-coders/skills/bugfix-doctor.description: Translates the error into plain English, then finds what caused it. It makes the smallest fix it can and checks that the fix worked.

/non-coders/skills/demo-prep.title: Demo Prep
/non-coders/skills/demo-prep.description: A timed demo script from problem to result, with a backup plan if the app breaks and the questions judges will likely ask.

/non-coders/skills/readme-writer.title: README Writer
/non-coders/skills/readme-writer.description: Writes your README (your repo's front page) with badges, a demo video, a how-it-works diagram, and team cards. It also fills in the repo's description, website, and topics so judges and recruiters can find it.

/blog.title: Blog
/blog.description: Hackathon strategy write-ups: how to win, pick a stack, pitch, and turn weekend projects into career wins.

/blog/what-to-do-after-a-hackathon.title: What to Do After a Hackathon: Ship 5 Assets That Get You Hired
/blog/what-to-do-after-a-hackathon.description: My first internship came from one LinkedIn post about a hackathon we didn't win. What to do after a hackathon: five linked assets, four written by AI skills.

/blog/hackathon-pitch-mistakes-la-hacks.title: 9 Hackathon Pitch Mistakes I Saw at LA Hacks
/blog/hackathon-pitch-mistakes-la-hacks.description: Judging LA Hacks, I watched good projects lose points to hackathon pitch mistakes. The one almost every team made was leaving the judges no time for Q&A.

/blog/how-to-win-hackathons.title: How to Win Hackathons: A Complete Guide from 36+ Victories
/blog/how-to-win-hackathons.description: How to win hackathons, in the seven phases I learned across 50+ events and 36+ wins: from picking your team to following up with people after judging ends.

/blog/best-tech-stack-for-hackathons.title: Best Tech Stack for Hackathons in 2026: Tools That Win Prizes
/blog/best-tech-stack-for-hackathons.description: The best tech stack for hackathons is the one your team already knows. If you don't have one yet, this is the Next.js, FastAPI, and Supabase default I use.

/blog/hackathon-tips-for-beginners.title: Hackathon Tips for Beginners: Your First Hackathon Survival Guide
/blog/hackathon-tips-for-beginners.description: You don't need an idea or a team to go to your first hackathon. These hackathon tips for beginners cover what to set up at home and how to spend the 24 hours.

/blog/hackathon-pitch-guide.title: Hackathon Pitch Guide: How to Present Your Project and Win Prizes
/blog/hackathon-pitch-guide.description: A hackathon pitch guide with one 3-minute structure: problem, live demo, how it works, and impact. Plus Q&A prep, and how to cut it down for a shorter slot.

/blog/non-coders-winning-hackathons.title: Non-Coders Winning Hackathons: What Domain Experts Bring
/blog/non-coders-winning-hackathons.description: A personal injury lawyer took 1st at Anthropic's hackathon without writing code. What that says about non-coders winning hackathons, and where coding helps.

/blog/build-with-elevenlabs-and-cursor.title: How to Build with ElevenLabs and Cursor at a Hackathon
/blog/build-with-elevenlabs-and-cursor.description: My loop for a voice AI hackathon project: write the PRD first, connect ElevenLabs to Cursor through MCP, then have the agent write each test before the feature.
